headline: An AI system in two UK hospitals decided on its own to discharge about a quarter to a third of urgent skin-cancer referrals, freeing thousands of specialist appointments, according to results shown at a dermatology congress.
score_reason: Real-world deployment data with notable results, but conference findings from two hospitals with some missed cancers; kept at 5.
importance_line: Patients on urgent skin cancer pathways and overstretched dermatology services stand to gain faster access, but six cancers were missed after discharge and the results are from two sites only.
summary: Scienmag, as relayed by Bioengineer.org, reports on findings presented at the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology congress: an autonomous AI system at two UK hospitals handled 8,391 urgent suspected skin cancer referrals and discharged benign cases without a dermatologist in 25% to 31% of patients. The researchers estimate it saved 2,851 clinician hours, but surveillance also found six cancers that had been wrongly discharged, and the authors call the results a proof of concept.
notes: Pool item credited HealthDay; its page gave no text, so the entry uses Bioengineer.org/Scienmag.
